verdicts.evidence: lines 400-430: every injected Copy button has a click listener that copies the block text; lines 444-454: each OS tab has click and keydown handlers that show its panel; TOC uses native details and anchors.
Static documentation page; no records, counts, metrics or charts are displayed.
One-screen page; no step depends on something entered on an earlier screen.
No inputs, forms or free text anywhere in the file.

lines 455-459: the only preselected value is the OS tab, taken from the saved choice or guessed from the platform; it only changes which install command is shown and loses nothing. No dialogs or default buttons.
lines 400-430: the frequent task, copying a command, is one click on the Copy button inside each block, with no other screen or dialog.

lines 337-340: a 'Try a restore now' callout not in the brief; lines 364-366: invented descriptions of the three next pages; line 299: added advice about opening a new terminal. Sections otherwise match the notes.
lines 144-150: all Copy buttons share one outlined secondary style; lines 168-173: tabs are plain. No button uses a filled primary style.
No control on the page deletes, overwrites or is irreversible; commands are only copied.
No disabled attribute or aria-disabled anywhere in markup or script.
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards in the file.
lines 256-367: all visible text concerns installing and using harbour; no mention of implementation, framework, the request or mock data.

lines 306-309: passphrase warning sits directly after the init command and names the action (save the passphrase); lines 337-340: restore note sits under the restore command and names an action (test a restore).

line 257: 'This page takes you from nothing installed to a first backup, a test restore, and a nightly schedule.' narrates the page itself; line 321 'In the rest of this page, use your s3:// address wherever you see...' also describes the page.

lines 256-257, 302, 324, 343: lede and section intros add information and do not restate their headings; lines 333 and 335 overlap slightly on the snapshot id but serve different points (where to get it, what to replace).
lines 256-367: heading 'Getting started', plain factual sentences, no exclamation marks, slogans or greeting; 'surest way' at line 339 is the only mild superlative and is tied to a concrete action.

line 405: button label 'Copy', changing to 'Copied' (410) or 'Select it' (414); each sits inside the one block it acts on and line 406 gives an accessible name including the command. Tabs are named for the OS they show.
lines 302, 330: 'repository' and 'snapshot' are defined in plain words; lines 351-358 show the tool's own error strings as the things the reader will see in the terminal, each explained.

lines 413-420: on copy failure the visible text is only the button label 'Select it' with the command selected; the full message 'Could not copy. The command is selected, press Ctrl or Command C.' is in the sr-only region (line 371). Verdicts differed on second pass.
line 415: 'Could not copy. The command is selected, press Ctrl or Command C.' is neutral, no blame, capitals or exclamation; line 307 warning title states the fact plainly.
No list, table, feed or search that can have zero items; all content is fixed.
No filters or search and nothing loads from a server.
Fully static page; script makes no network requests (lines 374-491).
No action or load takes longer than a moment; clipboard write and tab switching are immediate.
No asynchronous data, loading state or empty state.
Only fixed text is displayed; no variable-length data values.
The page holds no edits.
No form fields.
No form fields.
No form or validation.
No form that can reject input.
No form that can be rejected.
No form that can reject input.
No form or submit button.
No form with a server effect.
lines 409-412: Copy changes its label to 'Copied' and gains the done class as soon as the clipboard promise resolves; lines 434-441: a tab click swaps the panel and selected styling synchronously.
lines 410-412: success shows 'Copied' on the button; lines 413-420: failure changes the label to 'Select it' and selects the command text; lines 435-440: the chosen tab panel is shown in place.
lines 410-412: 'Copied' reports a clipboard write the user cannot otherwise see; there is no other success message.
lines 413-427: the copy-failure state ('Select it' label and the 'Could not copy...' status text) is reset by the same 2000 ms timer as success, so the error message auto-dismisses after two seconds.
No action removes, archives, moves or changes anything.
No irreversible action is performed by the page.
No confirmation dialogs.
No optimistic updates or background requests.
No modal dialogs.
No modal dialogs.
lines 256-270: h1 and one-paragraph lede, then requirements and the install step; the TOC is a narrow side column on desktop (line 85) and a collapsed details on narrow screens (lines 199, 464).
lines 227-270: a slim top bar, then 'Getting started', one lede paragraph and the requirements; no hero, greeting or window-height opening (h1 is 2.3rem, line 105).
No summary numbers, stat cards or charts.
No filtering, searching or sorting; the OS tabs are labelled tabs, not a filter over results.

Copy buttons are native buttons (lines 402-403); tabs use roving tabindex with Arrow, Home and End keys (lines 438, 446-453); TOC is a native details with links (lines 238-251); skip link at line 225. No focus trap.
line 173: selected tab has a 3px underline plus aria-selected; line 101: current TOC link is bold with a left bar; line 410: copied state changes the label text; line 307: warning has a text title.
line 371: div role=status aria-live=polite exists on load; lines 412, 415: copy success and failure text is written into it.
lines 273-275 and 437: tabs carry aria-selected that is updated on selection, with aria-controls; line 238: the TOC collapse is a native details element.

lines 193-213: under 860px the grid becomes one column, TOC collapses to a details, requirements stack; line 138: long commands scroll inside pre (min-width 0) with the Copy button kept beside; three tabs fit on one row.
lines 474-485: scroll spy sets class current and aria-current=location on the TOC link for the section in view; line 101 styles it bold with a left border as well as accent colour.

lines 443-445, 452: selecting an OS tab only writes localStorage and never updates the URL; the tabs and panels have no hash or query handling (lines 455-459), so a shared link cannot restore the chosen tab.
Single-view page; the only navigation is in-page anchors handled natively by the browser.

lines 236-253: TOC links to every section; lines 362-367: 'Where to go next' links to /docs/excludes, /docs/retention and /docs/check. (Brand and breadcrumb at lines 229-231 are plain text, not links.)
No dialogs or overlays.
The numbered sections are all on one scrolling page, not a stepped flow with next and back.

line 145: .copy has min-height 34px and padding 4px 12px, and the max-width 860px block (lines 193-213) does not enlarge it, so the page's most used control is 34px tall on phones. Tabs are 44px (line 170); TOC links about 38px (line 206).
line 88: the only sticky element is the TOC inside its own 210px grid column with max-height calc(100vh - 48px) and its own scroll, so it never overlaps main; line 198 makes it static under 860px.

lines 256-257: 'Getting started' followed by 'harbour makes encrypted, de-duplicated backups of your folders to a local disk or to any S3-compatible storage', which says what it is and for whom (people backing up their folders).
A documentation article with no main call to action for the visitor.
No images, illustrations, video or graphics in the file.
No testimonials, customer names, usage figures, ratings or prices.
No pricing section.
No images or video.
No announcement or promotional strip.
lines 400-430: every .cmd block gets a 'Copy' button with an aria-label naming the command; it copies code.textContent (prompts are CSS ::before, line 141, so excluded) and changes to 'Copied'.

lines 17-18: one teal accent used for links (55), focus ring (57), current TOC item (101), step numbers (115), selected tab (173) and next-page titles (190); amber and green (lines 21-24) are status colours only.
